Print or assert the count', 'If you mutate, assert the mutation actually applied', and 'A round-trip test over the real shipped artifacts ... pair it with adversarial fixtures'.
override.reason: The length is the standard's direct cost, not accidental sprawl. _installed_skills_root's 35 lines are one linear four-step resolution chain whose docstring states the order, plus the enumerate-every-root-tried refusal the handoff's criterion 5 requires; splitting it would scatter a decision that must be read in order. The mutation test's 47 lines are mostly the mandated self-assertions (the wrong root IS plausible; each target IS absent from it and IS present in the correct root) that stop an empty or mis-built fixture reporting clean. Extracting those would hide the very assertions the standard exists to force into view.

smells.finding: The two new test classes are focused and sized to their subject: GuardLocationStructureTests (pure predicate, lines 497-592) and GuardRuntimeTests (subprocess behaviour, 593-835). The split is along a real seam -- in-process predicate versus shelled-out run -- not an arbitrary cut. No production class was added.

CORPUS_MARKER = "CORPUS.json" is copied from install_constellation.py:1040 into verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py:18. The duplication is deliberate and defensible -- an installed bundle has no installer on its path -- but NOTHING asserts the two copies still agree. If the installer's marker is ever renamed, _is_skills_root silently stops matching by marker and degrades to clause 2 (the sibling-glob), which keeps working in the common case, so the drift would never surface as a failure. This is the shape the repo's own rule warns about: 'Define a guard by its consumer's behaviour, not by a hand-maintained list.' Observation, not a blocker -- a one-line test asserting the verifier's constant equals the installer's would close it, and the installer was correctly off-limits to this change.

The new helpers operate on their own Path argument and reach no further than one level (path, path.parent) to answer a question that is genuinely about that path's surroundings. No method is more interested in another object's data than its own.
No recurring group of parameters travels together. skills_root moves alone; work_id was already the sole identifier on each verify_* entry point.

skills_root is typed str | Path | None and normalized to a Path on the first line of the branch that uses it. That is an adapter at the CLI boundary -- argparse hands over a string -- not a primitive standing in for a missing type. Everything downstream is Path.
The longest signature added is two parameters (work_id, skills_root). _is_skills_root, _is_installed_bundle and _candidate_skills_roots take one or none.

Threading one new resolution option required edits at five parallel sites: verify_explorer, verify_commander, verify_admiral_prelaunch, the argparse declaration, and all three main() dispatch arms. The three verify_* functions are structurally identical -- read an artifact, resolve a root, load a verifier, translate the error -- and any further resolution option will have to be added to each in lockstep. Mild and localized to one module, so an observation rather than a blocker; a shared options object or a small dispatch table would make the next such change a single edit.
The module still changes for one reason -- how role artifacts are verified. Location resolution is a coherent part of that, and the change did not graft an unrelated axis of variation onto the file.

Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] is a pathlib construction chain on one value object, not a navigation chain across collaborators, and it is not new to this diff. No caller is asked to walk an object graph to reach what it needs.

Explicitly checked, because the pre-ruling made over-generalization the trap to avoid here. Nothing is built for a hypothetical caller: --skills-root has a named consumer in g4-integrate.c2 and I proved it is reachable and load-bearing rather than shipped-inert, and _candidate_skills_roots returns exactly the two scopes install_constellation.py already supports -- it mirrors an existing contract instead of inventing an extension point. No unused hook, no abstract base, no parameter without a caller.

_is_skills_root's docstring opens 'Decided by structure, never by name', but clause 2 does pattern-match a name -- path.glob('constellation-*') -- on the children. The consequence is not cosmetic: because the glob runs on the PARENT, a candidate named constellation-* that carries its own SKILL.md matches ITSELF, so _is_installed_bundle's parent clause is vacuous for exactly the directories the old name test used to accept, and the predicate collapses to 'has SKILL.md'. I confirmed this by building the case (decoy 3 in my k1 repro): a lone constellation-* directory with a SKILL.md in an otherwise ordinary parent is ACCEPTED. No real location is misjudged and the failure mode is a visible downstream refusal, so this is an observation, not a blocker -- but it is precisely the case the repo's rule covers: 'Assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it. Docstrings ... are hand-authored and none is checked against what runs.' The prose is stronger than the predicate.
